brief: Split at a separator or regular expression
description: Split <dataType> value into an array of strings, as ECMAScript's s.split(separator) does. separator is a string, which is literal text, or a regexp, which is a pattern. With a regexp, the text of each group of a match is put in the array after the piece before it (undefined when the group did not take part), and an empty match splits between code points but not at the start or end of the value.

parameters.description: Where to split: a string is literal text, a regexp is a pattern. If this is an empty string or separator is not specified, the value is split between characters. A regexp literal (/a+b/ or "a+b"re), to_regexp(s), or compile<regexp>(r) is already compiled; any other regexp value is compiled for this call.
parameters.name: separator

parameters.description: The maximum number of entries in the result. Any remaining part of value is ignored.
parameters.name: limit
